description: A single rendered table (Table 1) — no plots, micrographs or schematics are present in this group. The table reports "Element concentration (wt.%)" in columns Mn, Al, C, Nb, V, Mo, W and Fe, with three rows: 'specimen', 'γ' (austenite) and 'α' (ferrite). The 'specimen' row reads Mn 35.14, Al 5.97, C 0.095, Nb 0.11, V 0.10, Mo 1.24, W 0.95, Fe Bal. The 'γ' row reads Mn 35.92, Al 5.88, C 0.098, Nb 0.09, V 0.09, Mo 1.12, W 0.86, Fe Bal. The 'α' row reads Mn 32.44, Al 6.83, C "–" (dash, not reported), Nb 0.09, V 0.18, Mo 1.54, W 1.63, Fe Bal. Iron is printed only as "Bal." (balance) in every row, so no numeric Fe value exists in the figure; no units other than wt.% appear, and there are no error bars, colours or legends. The table's scientific role is compositional: it contrasts the bulk solution-treated specimen with the austenite and ferrite analysis, showing that α is Mn-depleted and Al-, V-, Mo- and W-enriched relative to γ, while carbon is reported for the bulk and γ but absent for α.

observations.observation: The table header reads 'Element concentration (wt.%)' and the column order is Mn, Al, C, Nb, V, Mo, W, Fe.
Row 'specimen' lists Mn 35.14, Al 5.97, C 0.095, Nb 0.11, V 0.10, Mo 1.24, W 0.95 and Fe as 'Bal.'.
Row 'γ' lists Mn 35.92, Al 5.88, C 0.098, Nb 0.09, V 0.09, Mo 1.12, W 0.86 and Fe as 'Bal.'.
Row 'α' lists Mn 32.44, Al 6.83, C as a dash ('–'), Nb 0.09, V 0.18, Mo 1.54, W 1.63 and Fe as 'Bal.'.
Relative to γ, the α row shows lower Mn (32.44 vs 35.92) and higher Al (6.83 vs 5.88), V (0.18 vs 0.09), Mo (1.54 vs 1.12) and W (1.63 vs 0.86) contents.
Carbon is printed for the 'specimen' (0.095) and 'γ' (0.098) rows but is replaced by a dash in the 'α' row, i.e. no carbon value is reported for ferrite in this table.
Iron is given only as 'Bal.' (balance) in all three rows, so the table contains no numeric Fe concentration.
The caption states that Table 1 presents the compositions (wt.%) of the steel measured by wet-chemical analysis.
The citing text states the ingot nominal composition is Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (wt.%), prepared by vacuum induction melting (50 kg) under high-purity Ar.
The citing text states that the austenite and ferrite compositions were estimated by electron probe microanalysis, with the carbon content calculated using the lever rule.
The citing text states the sample was solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h and oil quenched, and that the density measured by the Archimedes principle is 7.18 (unit truncated in the supplied text).

subfigures.description: A three-row composition table headed 'Element concentration (wt.%)' with columns Mn, Al, C, Nb, V, Mo, W, Fe; rows are 'specimen' (35.14 / 5.97 / 0.095 / 0.11 / 0.10 / 1.24 / 0.95 / Bal.), 'γ' (35.92 / 5.88 / 0.098 / 0.09 / 0.09 / 1.12 / 0.86 / Bal.) and 'α' (32.44 / 6.83 / – / 0.09 / 0.18 / 1.54 / 1.63 / Bal.).

unreadable_items: No numeric Fe concentration is printed: every Fe cell reads 'Bal.' (balance).
The α-row carbon cell contains only a dash ('–'), so no ferrite carbon value can be read from the table.
The table itself does not state the measurement methods; the wet-chemical analysis, EPMA and lever-rule attribution comes only from the caption and citing text.
